这篇文章是给刚到湾区的新移民、留学生、刚换工作搬来的人准备的。第一个月最容易乱的: This article is for new immigrants, international students, and people moving to the Bay Area for work. The first month can feel chaotic not because each task is hard, but because there are so many: housing, commuting, a phone plan, and everyday shopping. Putting them in order makes life easier.
第一周先把住和行稳定下来: Stabilize housing and transportation in the first week
刚到湾区，不建议一开始就把所有事情一次做完。第一目标是先把住处、出行和基本通讯稳: When you first arrive, don't try to do everything at once. Start by stabilizing your housing, transportation, and basic communication. With a reliable place to stay, opening a bank account, buying a car, finding a long-term rental, and getting to know the city become easier.
先确认临时住处或正式住处的入住安排，别落地当天才发现拿不到钥匙。: Confirm move-in arrangements for your temporary or permanent home. Don't wait until arrival day to discover you can't get the keys.
把常去的地点先存好：住处、学校、公司、超市、机场、最近的车站。: Save places you'll use often: home, school, work, groceries, the airport, and the nearest station.
先下载地图和常用打车、公交、外卖类应用，避免出门时手忙脚乱。: Download maps and commonly used ride, transit, and food-delivery apps first so you're not scrambling when you head out.
如果接下来两周都要跑看房或办事，先估一下自己更适合公交、拼车还是租车。: If the next two weeks involve viewings or appointments, consider whether transit, carpooling, or a rental car fits you best.
租房不要一上来就想一步到位: Your first rental doesn't have to be your forever fit
很多新来湾区的人会急着马上签长期房，但如果你对通勤、城市差异、生活圈还没感觉，先: Newcomers often feel pressure to sign a long lease immediately. But if you're still learning the commute, city differences, and daily routines, some observation time can be the steadier choice. The most useful first-month goal is not finding a perfect home—it's learning which area, commute, and budget work for you.
先用 1 到 2 周感受通勤，再决定是不是要住得离公司或学校更近。: Try the commute for 1 to 2 weeks before deciding whether you need to live closer to work or school.
看房时不要只看房间本身，也要看晚上回家路线、超市距离和停车情况。: When viewing a place, check more than the room: look at the route home at night, grocery access, and parking.
合租要提前问清楚厨房、洗衣、访客、作息和分账方式。: Before sharing a home, ask about the kitchen, laundry, guests, schedules, and splitting expenses.
涉及押金、合同、申请流程等内容，建议以合同和官方信息为准。: For deposits, contracts, and application procedures, refer to the contract and official information.
手机、支付和日常采购先走简单路线: Keep phone service, payments, and everyday shopping simple at first
第一个月不要急着把所有生活配置拉满。手机先解决可用，支付先解决顺手，家里用品先解: Don't rush to set up everything in your first month. Start with a working phone, convenient payments, and enough household essentials. Buying too much, opening too many accounts, and moving too fast can waste time and money.
手机先确认本地号码和流量能正常用，方便看房、联系学校公司和收验证码。: Make sure your local phone number and mobile data work so you can arrange viewings, contact school or work, and receive verification codes.
买生活用品时先从基础开始：被子、洗漱、简单厨具、转换插头、清洁用品。: Start household shopping with basics: bedding, toiletries, simple cookware, plug adapters, and cleaning supplies.
如果暂时没有车，优先住在买菜方便、离车站不太远的地方。: Without a car, prioritize convenient grocery shopping and a reasonably nearby transit stop.
第一个月先建立一个固定补货点，比如常去超市、药店和附近快递点。: Establish regular places to restock during your first month, such as a supermarket, pharmacy, and nearby shipping location.
通勤和生活半径要尽快摸清: Get to know your commute and everyday surroundings soon
湾区地图看起来不大，但城市之间通勤差异很明显。你需要尽快弄清楚自己是依赖 BAR: The Bay Area may look small on a map, but commutes vary considerably between cities. Find out whether you'll rely on BART, Caltrain, driving, or a mix. Look beyond distance to transfers, parking, late returns, and the last mile.
第一个月最值回票价的动作: One of the most useful things to do in your first month
挑两个工作日，用你以后可能真的会用的路线去跑一次通勤。纸面上看 30 分钟，实际: Choose two weekdays and try a route you might actually use to commute. A trip that looks like 30 minutes on paper can become 55 with waiting, walking, and finding parking. That experience can be more useful than reading a guide.
刚到湾区的前几周，很多判断都会变。你原本觉得想住市中心，可能后来更在意安静和停车: Your preferences may change in your first few weeks. You might arrive wanting downtown life and later value quiet and parking, or plan to drive and discover the commuter train is easier. Get everyday life working, then improve it gradually. You don't need to decide everything in week one.
